holidays.name: National Dog Biscuit Day
holidays.description: A day to give your four-legged best friend a crunchy treat, whether it's store-bought or homemade. Tail wags are the whole point.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and no single founder is clearly credited. It celebrates the humble dog biscuit, a treat that has been around since the 1800s.
holidays.funFact: The first commercial dog biscuit is usually credited to James Spratt, an American electrician who was in London in the 1860s. He reportedly got the idea after watching dogs gobble up leftover ship biscuits at the docks.

holidays.name: National Banana Bread Day
holidays.description: A salute to the bread that rescues overripe, spotty bananas from the trash. Bake a loaf, slice it thick and add butter if you like.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday of unclear origin. Banana bread became a household staple in the 1930s. Chemical leaveners like baking soda were newly common then, and thrifty cooks wanted to use up ripe fruit.
holidays.funFact: Banana bread is often said to have taken off during the Great Depression. Home bakers hated wasting food, so they turned bananas that were past their prime into a cake-like loaf.

holidays.name: National Tootsie Roll Day
holidays.description: A chewy, chocolatey tribute to one of America's classic candies. It's a good excuse to dig through the Halloween-style candy bowl for a Tootsie Roll.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial candy observance. It honors the Tootsie Roll, created in 1896 by Austrian immigrant Leo Hirshfield in New York City.
holidays.funFact: Hirshfield named the candy after his daughter, whose nickname was Tootsie. Tootsie Rolls were also a handy ration for US soldiers in World War II because they resist melting and keep well.
